newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan court declares realtor president bankrupt.
newsitem.headline: Japan court declares realtor president bankrupt.

text.p: The president of Osaka-based unlisted realtor Tanimachi Fudosan has been declared bankrupt by the Osaka District Court with debts of about 160 billion yen, the court said on Wednesday.
Private research firm Tokyo Shoko Research said Tanimachi president Nobuo Sawayama was a major borrower from "jusen" or failed mortgage firms.
But the court did not say whether Sawayama's debts had resulted from jusen borrowing. A court spokesman said Sawayama was declared bankrupt on December 20.
Tokyo Shoko said Sawayama's debts included loan guarantees for companies with which Tanimachi has close ties.
A finance company in the Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd group had extended four billion yen worth of loans to Sawayama, Tokyo Shoko said.
Tokyo Shoko said that it did not know about the other creditors.
Sawayama's lawyer was not immediately available for comment.
A Tanimachi official said Sawayama resigned last month and the company is doing business normally. He said the company could not comment on Sawayama's personal debts.
